profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer and sports enthusiast.
I have had the pleasure to work on great products with talented people, at Google, Pandora, Twitter, Ask.com, and IBM. I am a hard-working, result-oriented professional. I enjoy solving complex problems and building quality software solutions.

Skills:

Languages:  Java, C++, Scala, Python, Javascript, Ruby, Bash, JUnit, Mockito, ScalaTest
Server Frameworks:  gRPC, Netty, Jetty, Tomcat, Apache, Nginx, Finagle, Guice, Spring
Structured Data:  Protobuf, Thrift, Textproto, JSON, YAML, XML
Data Store:  Spanner, MySQL, Postgres, Hibernate, Hive, Hadoop, AWS DynamoDB
Cache & PubSub:  Redis, Memcached, PubSub, Kafka, Kestrel
Template:  Mustache, Velocity, JSP, Bootstrap
Build & Version:  Git, Gradle, Maven

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Project lead of design and launch of backend data services within YouTube Metadata Service (YTMS), a core application infrastructure that serves metadata for YouTube core entities, e.g. videos, playlists, and channels. New services provided indexing and serving of signal data to be used in discovery and recommendation pipelines.
Designed and implemented RPC-based real-time indexing of video uploads into YTMS. Implemented and launched improved indexing cache replication via PubSub and RPC. YTMS backend code written in C++ and Python.
Joined Google Meet’s Video Core team. Implemented improved End Conference for All within Meetings API Server (MAS), a core application infrastructure for Google Meet. MAS backend code written in Java. Project lead of design and integration of Converged Group Calling into MAS, to support migration of the Duo calling app into new Meet app for both calling and meetings.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Tech lead of a cross-functional engineering team focused on building features for user music libraries, playlists, and stations. Pandora Premium feature started with My Music page, which was powered by this music library service.
Server lead for backend services providing persistent storage and APIs for user music libraries and playlists. Tech stack consisted of JSON, Java 8, Jetty, Redis, Postgres. Included StatsD and Graphite for observability. Provided data pipelines built with Kafka and Hive, to deliver user data updates to other backends. Delivered APIs to support a wide range of platforms, including mobile, web, voice-enabled devices, TV/cable boxes, Alexa, Sonos, etc.

positions.title: Founder
positions.description: Created a new Android mobile app. Built a Java backend for the app, using Amazon Web Services. AWS services included Route 53, S3, DynamoDB, EC2, ELB, Auto Scaling, and CodeDeploy. Built a HTTP server from scratch, using Netty 4, to serve web content and API requests. Web pages used Mustache templates, Bootstrap, and JQuery. REST API used JSON payloads. Persistent data was stored in DynamoDB tables. Backend included automated scheduled jobs using Quartz. Built the Android app using Android Studio, Genymotion, Fabric (Crashlytics), and Google Analytics.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Service owner of the tweet scheduling system that allowed users to reliably post tweets at a future time. Feature was available in TweetDeck and Twitter for Business. Brand managers and advertisers relied on tweet scheduling. Tech stack consisted of HTTP/Thrift/Finagle/MySQL.
Contributed to the design and implementation of Twitter's infrastructure HTTP framework. The Twitter web site and REST API were built on this HTTP framework, written in Scala using Finagle. Ported the tweet, retweet, and new user API endpoints from Ruby on Rails to Scala and Finagle services.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Designed and developed a new web framework, using Jetty, Velocity templates, Apache HTTP client, Spring IoC, and Spring MVC. Development lead for the SEM & SEO engineering team, building new web pages and ad configurations. Built a data aggregation service using Jetty and Java to provide the XML feeds that powered Ask.com search results.
